title: Learning a Rotation Invariant Detector with Rotatable Bounding Box

problem.summary: Traditional axis-aligned bounding boxes are rotation-variant, so detectors fail on arbitrarily oriented objects such as ships, vehicles and airplanes in aerial/satellite images, mixing background into the box and failing to separate dense nearby targets.
statements: The traditional bounding box is rotation variant and poorly suits objects whose orientation varies.
Box width/height do not reflect the physical size of rotated targets, so customized prior boxes are meaningless.
Around 60% of a ship's axis-aligned box can be background pixels when the ship is near 45 degrees.
Dense objects are hard to separate with axis-aligned boxes, and existing detectors lack rotation invariance.

evidence.quote: The traditional bounding box is a rotation variant data structure, which becomes a shortcoming when the detector has to deal with orientation variations of target objects.
BBox meets difficulties locating objects with different orientation angles.
about 60% region inside the BBox belongs to background pixels when the orientation angle of the ship is near 45 degrees
the existing detection methods suffer from the lack of rotation invariant property

background.summary: The work builds on the R-CNN/Fast/Faster R-CNN lineage and on box-based one-stage detectors SSD and YOLO, plus prior attempts at rotation invariance (rotation-invariant regularization, Oriented Response Networks), claiming those either eliminate rotation at feature level or cannot be used directly as detectors.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.quote: Instead of using SS to generate region proposals, Faster R-CNN applies region proposal networks (RPNs) to generate the proposals [19]

relatedWork.name: SSD
relatedWork.relation: box-based one-stage baseline benchmarked against DRBox
relatedWork.quote: We refer to YOLO and SSD as box-based methods since they generate several boxes for detecting objects in the image according to certain rules.

relatedWork.name: ORN (Oriented Response Networks)
relatedWork.relation: prior orientation-extracting network, but image classification rather than detection
relatedWork.quote: Zhou et al. proposed a network named ORN [27] which shows similar character with our method.

relatedWork.name: FPN
relatedWork.relation: prior work that reuses the pyramidal feature hierarchy via lateral connections
relatedWork.quote: The feature pyramid network (FPN) [15] better utilizes the pyramidal feature hierarchy

evidence.quote: Most existing detection methods use bounding box to locate objects in images.
Unlike these methods which try to eliminate the effect of rotation on the feature level, we prefer to make the rotation information useful for feature extraction

solution.summary: The paper defines a rotatable bounding box (RBox) with an angle parameter and builds DRBox, a SSD-style detector whose multi-angle prior RBoxes, ArIoU-based sample assignment and tangent angle regression make the network predict orientation while remaining rotation invariant.
solution.approach: Replace axis-aligned BBoxes with 5-parameter RBoxes, slide and rotate prior RBoxes over the image, train with angle-related IoU (ArIoU) plus a tangent angle regression term, and infer with standard IoU NMS.
components: rotatable bounding box (RBox) with center, width, height and angle
multi-angle prior RBoxes at each location (e.g. 0:30:330 degrees)
ArIoU for positive sample assignment and training
tangent-based angle regression term in the loss
pyramid input: rescale image and split into overlapped 300x300 sub-images
truncated VGG backbone ending at conv4_3

evidence.quote: a new detection method is proposed which applies the newly defined rotatable bounding box (RBox).
The training of DRBox forces the detection networks to learn the correct orientation angle of the objects, so that the rotation invariant property can be achieved.
Each sub-task focuses on one narrow angle range, therefore decreases the difficulty caused by rotation of objects.
A prior RBox P is assigned to a ground truth RBox G when ArIoU(P, G) > 0.5.

experiments.summary: Since no open satellite detection dataset existed, the authors built a GoogleEarth dataset of vehicles, ships and airplanes, then compared DRBox with Faster R-CNN and SSD using precision-recall curves, BEP/AP/mAP, and rotation-robustness metrics (STD AP, STD AS).

evidence.quote: The results shows that DRBox performs much better than traditional bounding box based methods do on the given tasks
DRBox is always the best on all the indexes compared with SSD and Faster R-CNN.
The P-R curve of SSD and Faster R-CNN are always below the P-R curve of DRBox.

limitations.summary: The evaluation relies on a self-built, non-public dataset with separate per-category models, and the fixed receptive field and feature map resolution bound the sizes of detectable objects.
items: No open-source satellite detection dataset was available, so the evaluation uses a self-built GoogleEarth dataset.
Three separate DRBox networks are trained, one per object category (vehicle, ship, airplane).
Receptive field of 108x108 pixels means larger targets cannot be detected.
conv4_3 feature map is 38x38, so targets closer than 8 pixels may be missed.
Faster R-CNN is slightly more robust to rotation on airplane targets.

evidence.quote: The receptive field of DRBox is 108 pixels 108 pixels, so any targets larger than this scope cannot be detected.
the feature map of layer conv4 3 is 38 × 38, so the targets closer than 8 pixels may be missed.
We have not found any open source dataset on this problem, so we build one using the GoogleEarth images.

futureDirections.direction: Integrate RBox into proposal-based detectors such as R-FCN or Faster R-CNN.
futureDirections.quote: DRBox is designed as a box-based method, whereas it is also possible to apply RBox into proposal based detection frameworks, e.g. R-FCN or Faster R-CNN.

futureDirections.direction: Reuse the multi-scale local orientation information learned with RBox for other orientation-sensitive tasks.
futureDirections.quote: We are looking forward of this interesting property to be used in other orientation sensitive tasks.

datasets: GoogleEarth satellite images (self-built: ~12000 vehicles, 3000 ships, 2000 airplanes)

equations.name: ArIoU
equations.expr: ArIoU(A,B) = (area(A_hat ∩ B) / area(A_hat ∪ B)) * cos(θA − θB)

applications.detail: DRBox detects vehicles, ships and airplanes in satellite imagery; hundreds of remote sensing satellites generate huge image volumes yearly.
applications.quote: A typical application is the object detection task in aerial and satellite images.

applications.detail: Predicted car head directions on roads match the prior knowledge that traffic keeps to the right, showing orientation output is usable downstream.
applications.quote: The estimated direction of cars on road matches the prior knowledge that traffic always keeps to the right of the road.

deploymentClaims: DRBox reaches 70-80 fps on NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti and Intel Core i7.
Pyramid input costs no more than 4/3 times extra time; effective throughput is 1600x1600 pixels^2 per second.
SSD and Faster R-CNN run at 70 fps and 20 fps respectively on the same dataset and architecture.

evidence.quote: DRBox reaches 70-80 fps on NVIDIA GTX 1080Ti and Intel Core i7.
The speed of SSD and Faster R-CNN are 70 fps and 20 fps on our dataset using the same convolution network architecture.
